This was on the same day as other [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|local elections]]. ==Summary== ===Background=== At the [[2021 East Sussex County Council election|2021 election]], the Conservatives won an outright majority of seats.{{Cite news |date=2021-05-07 |title=Elections 2021: Conservatives hold Sussex county councils |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-sussex-57023007 |access-date=2024-11-29 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}} After two 2023 by-elections following the deaths of sitting Conservative councillors the party lost overall control of the council.{{Cite news |date=2023-08-04 |title=Tories lose overall control of county council |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cjq145xygj3o |access-date=2026-04-12 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}} The election is expected to be the last before the council is abolished and replaced with new unitary authorities.{{Cite news |date=2026-03-09 |title=Is political upheaval coming in Sussex this May|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cn8zdxlw1y4o |access-date=2026-04-12 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}} The election was originally postponed from 2025, then again delayed by another year until the government u-turned and reinstated the elections for 2026.{{Cite news |date=2026-02-16 |title=Government abandons plans to delay 30 council elections|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c70ne31d884o|access-date=2026-04-15 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}} The Conservatives and Labour Party are expected to be tested heavily due to the growth of Reform UK (notably high polling, a by-election win and a defection from the Conservatives) and the Green Party (who control councils since 2023 in Hastings, Lewes and Wealden) since the last election in 2021.
